  that exact name appears in `project_map(path)` output for the file.
  If it isn't there, don't use it — grep elsewhere or ask "the
  only things I see in that file are X, Y, Z — which did you mean?".

  shows `mark_compacted`, do not answer with `compact` — different
  names.
- The `imports: ...` line in `project_map(path)` output is GROUND TRUTH for
  intra-project dependencies. If X's imports don't list Y, then X
  doesn't use Y — never claim or draw otherwise.

  like a dataclass / BaseModel — you might "know" the body, you do
  not. Call read_file before reproducing more than a signature.
  (A separate HOOK rejects code blocks emitted without a prior read.)

  answer second.

  "I meant …", "specifically …"), do NOT recycle the previous
  turn — your prior answer missed the thing. Run NEW tool calls

  algorithm" by repeating session.py instead of grep'ing `compact`
  to locate StepAgent.compact().

  `A[Label] --> B`, `A{Decision} -->|yes| B`, `A --- B`.

  inter-object calls). Syntax: `participant Alice`,

  public API). Syntax: `class Name { +method() +field: int }`,
  `Parent <|-- Child`, `Container *-- Item`, `Owner o-- Asset`.

- Insert: `write_file(path, content, insert_after_line=N)`. Use 0 to prepend.

line numbers, then write_file with the range. Never use shell_exec / echo /
heredocs to write files.

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test suite via the active SkillRegistry skill (pytest, docker, …). Returns exit code + truncated output.

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python

## Описание
Этот проект представляет собой простой Python-CLI для управления заметками. Он позволяет добавлять, просматривать, искать и удалять заметки с использованием JSON-хранилища.

python notes/cli.py list

python notes/cli.py search "заметка"
```

### delete
Удаляет заметку по её индексу.

**Пример использования:**
```bash
python notes/cli.py delete 1
```

from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve

Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    storage = Storage()

        storage.add(args.note)

        for i, note in enumerate(notes):

    elif args.command == 'search':

        for i, note in enumerate(results):

• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).

• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

function.name: write_file

• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':

function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:

• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

function.description:

• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python
function.description: Evaluate a short Python snippet in the project directory and return stdout+stderr+exit. Repl-style probe — use to verify a debug hypothesis without writing to disk: `import x; print(type(x.y))` or `from mod import f; f('test')`. Same sandbox as shell_exec. Prefers `.venv/bin/python` if present; falls back to `python3` (NOT `python` — Debian/Ubuntu often lacks that symlink). function.name: shell_exec

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test suite via the active SkillRegistry skill (pytest, docker, …). Returns exit code + truncated output.

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python

Single snippet per call, no multi-statement scripts beyond a handful of lines — for those use write_file + run_tests.

function.name: shell_exec

Hard-blocked from rm -rf /, dd of=/dev/*, mkfs, sudo, pipe-to-shell, and fork bombs even in optimist mode. Returns combined stdout+stderr and the exit code.

{"path":"notes/cli.py","content":"import argparse
from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

function.name: grep

Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

Этот проект представляет собой простой Python-CLI для управления заметками. Он позволяет добавлять, просматривать, искать и удалять заметки с использованием JSON-хранилища.

## Команды

### add
Добавляет новую заметку.

**Пример использования:**
```bash
python notes/cli.py add "Это моя первая заметка"
```

### list
Выводит список всех заметок.

**Пример использования:**
```bash
python notes/cli.py list
```

### search
Ищет заметки по ключевым словам.

**Пример использования:**
```bash
python notes/cli.py search "заметка"
```

### delete
Удаляет заметку по её индексу.

**Пример использования:**
```bash
python notes/cli.py delete 1
```
"}

{"path":"notes/cli.py","content":"import argparse
from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test suite via the active SkillRegistry skill (pytest, docker, …). Returns exit code + truncated output.

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python
function.description: Evaluate a short Python snippet in the project directory and return stdout+stderr+exit. Repl-style probe — use to verify a debug hypothesis without writing to disk: `import x; print(type(x.y))` or `from mod import f; f('test')`. Same sandbox as shell_exec. Prefers `.venv/bin/python` if present; falls back to `python3` (NOT `python` — Debian/Ubuntu often lacks that symlink). Single snippet per call, no multi-statement scripts beyond a handful of lines — for those use write_file + run_tests.

snippet.description: Python source to feed to `python -c`. Newlines OK. Tip: prefix with imports the verification needs.

function.name: shell_exec
function.description: Run an arbitrary shell command in the project root. Useful for mass edits (sed/awk/find) or git plumbing that SEARCH/REPLACE would be a waste for. Hard-blocked from rm -rf /, dd of=/dev/*, mkfs, sudo, pipe-to-shell, and fork bombs even in optimist mode. Returns combined stdout+stderr and the exit code.

command.description: Full shell command to run, as it would be typed in a terminal. Quote strings as needed; do NOT prepend `bash -c`.

from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test suite via the active SkillRegistry skill (pytest, docker, …). Returns exit code + truncated output.

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python
function.description: Evaluate a short Python snippet in the project directory and return stdout+stderr+exit. Repl-style probe — use to verify a debug hypothesis without writing to disk: `import x; print(type(x.y))` or `from mod import f; f('test')`. Same sandbox as shell_exec. Prefers `.venv/bin/python` if present; falls back to `python3` (NOT `python` — Debian/Ubuntu often lacks that symlink). Single snippet per call, no multi-statement scripts beyond a handful of lines — for those use write_file + run_tests.

snippet.description: Python source to feed to `python -c`. Newlines OK. Tip: prefix with imports the verification needs.

function.name: shell_exec
function.description: Run an arbitrary shell command in the project root. Useful for mass edits (sed/awk/find) or git plumbing that SEARCH/REPLACE would be a waste for. Hard-blocked from rm -rf /, dd of=/dev/*, mkfs, sudo, pipe-to-shell, and fork bombs even in optimist mode. Returns combined stdout+stderr and the exit code.

command.description: Full shell command to run, as it would be typed in a terminal. Quote strings as needed; do NOT prepend `bash -c`.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Load a skill to get stack-specific guidance — exact test/lint/format commands and project rules. Call early on a coding task once you know the stack (e.g. saw pyproject.toml → load_skill('python')). See the 'Available skills' catalog in the system prompt for valid names.

function.name: unload_skill
function.description: Unload a previously loaded skill when it's no longer relevant for the current task. Frees context for unrelated work.

name.description: Skill name to unload.

{"path":"notes/cli.py","content":"import argparse
from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

from .storage import Storage

def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='CLI для заметок')
    subparsers = parser.add_subparsers(dest='command', help='Доступные команды')

    # Команда add
    add_parser = subparsers.add_parser('add', help='Добавить новую заметку')
    add_parser.add_argument('note', type=str, help='Текст заметки')

    # Команда list
    list_parser = subparsers.add_parser('list', help='Вывести список всех заметок')

    # Команда search
    search_parser = subparsers.add_parser('search', help='Искать заметки по ключевым словам')
    search_parser.add_argument('keyword', type=str, help='Ключевое слово для поиска')

    # Команда delete
    delete_parser = subparsers.add_parser('delete', help='Удалить заметку по её индексу')
    delete_parser.add_argument('index', type=int, help='Индекс заметки для удаления')

    args = parser.parse_args()

    storage = Storage()

    if args.command == 'add':
        storage.add(args.note)
    elif args.command == 'list':
        notes = storage.list()
        for i, note in enumerate(notes):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'search':
        results = storage.search(args.keyword)
        for i, note in enumerate(results):
            print(f'{i}: {note}')
    elif args.command == 'delete':
        storage.delete(args.index)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
"}

function.name: read_file
function.description:
Read the body of a file with 1-based line numbers. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• whole file: just `path` (caps at 400 lines, then `… N more lines` footer).
• window: `path` + `start_line` and/or `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Use after a project_map hit or a failing-test line number — drops you straight onto the region.
• find: `path` + `find=<substring>` returns every match plus `context` lines around it (default 20), merged into non-overlapping windows. Use when you want to read around a name without knowing its line.
Heavy — use only when you need the actual code. For 'what's in this file', use `project_map(path=...)`.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

start_line.description: Optional. 1-based start of the window. If omitted but end_line is set, defaults to 1.

end_line.description: Optional. 1-based end of the window (inclusive). If omitted, extends to start_line + 400 or end of file.

find.description: Optional substring search. Returns every hit plus `context` lines around it. Mutually exclusive with the window args.

context.description: Optional lines-of-context for `find` mode (default 20). Ignored without `find`.

function.name: write_file
function.description:
Write to a file. Three modes — pick by which args you pass:
• overwrite/create: `path` + `content`. Replaces the whole file (creates if missing). Use for new files and small rewrites.
• replace lines: `path` + `content` + `start_line` + `end_line` (1-based, inclusive). Replaces only those lines. Use for surgical edits in large files.
• insert: `path` + `content` + `insert_after_line` (1-based; use 0 to prepend). Inserts the content after that line.
Always pass the literal content — newlines preserved. Use this instead of shell_exec for any file write.

path.description: Relative path from the project root.

content.description: File content as a single string. In overwrite mode: the whole file. In replace/insert mode: just the chunk to put in.

start_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based first line to replace (inclusive). Requires `end_line`.

end_line.description: Replace mode: 1-based last line to replace (inclusive). Requires `start_line`.

insert_after_line.description: Insert mode: 1-based line number to insert AFTER. Use 0 to prepend at the top. Mutually exclusive with start_line/end_line.

function.name: project_map
function.description: See what's in the project — files, classes, functions, methods. No bodies. Without `path` — a list of files with line counts. With `path` set to a file — that file's classes/functions/methods with their signatures and imports (no implementation). Prefer this over `read_file` for 'what's there' questions; reach for read_file only when you need the actual code body.

path.description: Optional file or directory path.

function.name: goto_definition
function.description: Find where a top-level name is defined: class, function, or method. Returns each definition site as `path:line  kind  qualified_name` — straight pointer with no body, no signature dump. Call this when the user asks WHERE a specific symbol is defined / lives. Cheaper and more precise than grep — grep returns every textual mention; this returns only the def. If nothing matches, fall back to grep for a broader lexical search.

name.description: Exact identifier to look up. No dots, no parens. For 'where is Class.method', pass just `method` and read the qualified_name column to disambiguate which class owns it.

function.name: find_references
function.description: List every line in the project that mentions `name` as a whole word. Returns `path:line: code` rows, capped to 50. This is the 'where is X USED?' tool — paired with goto_definition (the 'where is X DEFINED?' tool). Includes imports and comments because users routinely ask 'where does X get imported' or 'who has a TODO about X' — both legitimate references that AST-only search would miss.

name.description: Exact identifier; word-bounded match.

function.name: grep
function.description: Search the project (or a subdirectory) for a regex pattern. Returns up to 30 matching lines. Call this whenever the user asks WHERE / FIND / IS THERE something, or before answering a 'does X exist' question. Prefer grep over read_file when you don't yet know which file holds the symbol.

path.description: Optional relative path. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: retrieve
function.description: Search the project for symbols (classes, functions, methods) whose name or docstring matches keywords from `query`. Returns top-10 ranked hits as `path:line  kind  qualified_name  · docstring`. Use when you know roughly WHAT you want but not the exact symbol name — fuzzier than `goto_definition`, more structured than `grep`. Optional `path` narrows the search to one file.

query.description: Free-text keywords. Split on whitespace + punctuation; tokens are matched case-insensitively against symbol names and docstrings.

path.description: Optional relative path to scope the search to one file. Omit to search the whole project.

function.name: run_tests
function.description: Run the project's test suite via the active SkillRegistry skill (pytest, docker, …). Returns exit code + truncated output.

args.description: Optional pytest args (e.g. 'tests/test_x.py' or '-k name'). Empty to run everything.

function.name: run_python
function.description: Evaluate a short Python snippet in the project directory and return stdout+stderr+exit. Repl-style probe — use to verify a debug hypothesis without writing to disk: `import x; print(type(x.y))` or `from mod import f; f('test')`. Same sandbox as shell_exec. Prefers `.venv/bin/python` if present; falls back to `python3` (NOT `python` — Debian/Ubuntu often lacks that symlink). Single snippet per call, no multi-statement scripts beyond a handful of lines — for those use write_file + run_tests.

snippet.description: Python source to feed to `python -c`. Newlines OK. Tip: prefix with imports the verification needs.

function.name: shell_exec
function.description: Run an arbitrary shell command in the project root. Useful for mass edits (sed/awk/find) or git plumbing that SEARCH/REPLACE would be a waste for. Hard-blocked from rm -rf /, dd of=/dev/*, mkfs, sudo, pipe-to-shell, and fork bombs even in optimist mode. Returns combined stdout+stderr and the exit code.

command.description: Full shell command to run, as it would be typed in a terminal. Quote strings as needed; do NOT prepend `bash -c`.

function.name: load_skill
function.description: Load a skill to get stack-specific guidance — exact test/lint/format commands and project rules. Call early on a coding task once you know the stack (e.g. saw pyproject.toml → load_skill('python')). See the 'Available skills' catalog in the system prompt for valid names.

name.description: Skill name from the catalog, e.g. 'python', 'go', 'js'.

function.name: unload_skill
function.description: Unload a previously loaded skill when it's no longer relevant for the current task. Frees context for unrelated work.

name.description: Skill name to unload.
